item.description: - **Desktop widgets**: add Dashbar from the widget gallery (right-click the desktop, Edit Widgets). The small one shows Claude's 5-hour and weekly limits and when they reset, the medium one each tool's limits and how many agents are working. When Dashbar isn't running they dim and say since when

- An account whose folder doesn't exist no longer counts as a second account, so Dashbar stops naming everything "Claude · Personal" when you only use one. Settings → Accounts marks it "Folder not found" and keeps it, and Dashbar starts reading it within a minute of the folder appearing - A permission prompt that was settled some other way, by the app you run Claude Code in or by Claude Code denying it on its own, now leaves Dashbar's notch and panel straight away instead of staying until its timer runs out

- **The dashbar command**: type `dashbar` in Terminal to see which agents need you, which are working and how much of each plan limit is left, or put `dashbar line` in your tmux status bar or shell prompt. It reads what Dashbar already shows, so Dashbar has to be running. Homebrew adds it to your PATH; with the DMG, copy the command from Settings → Integrations - **A notification when a used-up limit resets**: once a 5-hour or Weekly limit has been used up, Dashbar tells you when it resets so you can pick up where you left off. It's covered by the same setting, now "When a plan limit runs low or resets" - The Claude Code status line script no longer writes session ids to disk. Dashbar updates the script by itself the next time it opens - `brew uninstall --cask --zap dashbar` now also removes Dashbar's caches
